column7: Browne introduced ATOM as the green side of the Protein Dual Overdrive sold as a standalone pedal; its stated lineage begins from the ODR-1 family but the builder says it is not an ODR-1 clone. Identifying traits include lowered gain, restored mids, tightened low end, redesigned power section for sag/feel, soft switching and Flat Dark Earth finish.
column10: Standalone ATOM should remain linked to the Protein green-side lineage without collapsing its product identity into Protein.

column7: Browne announced Gritador in June 2023. Builder describes nuanced midrange, slightly less symmetrical clipping and a fuller but tight low end. Compact enclosure, 9V operation and soft switching are documented in the release.
column10: Useful external identifiers are the Bullfrog Belly Green finish, control layout and the builder's explicit 2023 release date.

column7: Lollar's first effects pedal was a limited run of 100 made with KGR Harmony Effects. The cast-iron enclosure used a nambu-tekki-inspired finish/process, with Volume, Gain and a three-band EQ. The run sold out in three hours and Lollar said it did not plan an immediate repeat.
column10: Treat Lollar as marketed brand and KGR Harmony Effects as collaborating builder/manufacturing participant until stronger primary attribution is found.

column7: Nemetone announced Distiny in July 2023 as a hand-built Canadian overdrive/distortion pedal with a two-position Soft/Hard operating-mode switch. The product was designed to cover a broad range from soft overdrive to heavy distortion with few controls.
column10: Primary builder documentation still needs to be found; preserve Canadian hand-built attribution from the launch coverage.

column7: Cornerstone introduced Colosseum in 2023 after gathering customer input. It combines independently usable Blues Breaker and Klon-style sections, adds a clean control on the BB side, Clip Blender on the Klon side, four rear I/O jacks and switchable channel order.
column10: Keep Colosseum as a distinct product while linking it to the Gladio/Antique/Klon-style family relationships it explicitly uses.

column7: EQD brought back White Light as a Legacy Reissue in March 2023. The documented modern version has Gain, Weight, Level and a Compression switch, with Flexi-Switch relay bypass and 9V operation; EQD now lists it as no longer in production.
column10: This is an edition/reissue identity, not a new White Light generation. Preserve its 2023 reissue date separately from the original White Light history.
